title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens a new section of the 'Longue Marche' continuation: '1°) Action différentiable et groupes de Teichmüller spéciaux'. The previous pages dealt with adelic and Lie-type envelopes of profinite groups. Here Grothendieck sets up a purely differentiable, topological construction. Its purpose is to define 'special' Teichmüller groups, meaning groups that remember a tangent direction at each marked point.

Setting:
- X is a connected, orientable differentiable surface, compact in the case of interest.
- I is a discrete subset of X (the marked points).
- For each i in I, S_i is the space of tangent half-lines at i. This is the circle of directions, i.e. the boundary circle of the real oriented blow-up of X at i.
- S̃_i is a universal cover of S_i.
- S = S_I is the disjoint union of the S_i, and S̃ is the disjoint union of the S̃_i.

A diffeomorphism u of the pair (X,I) acts on S through its derivative. Call this action u_S; it may permute the circles if u permutes I. Grothendieck considers the set of lifts ũ of u_S to S̃.

The orientation module T_0 is π_1 of a circle of directions, which is Z twisted by orientation. It acts on each S̃_i as the deck group, and S̃/T_0 ≅ S. Hence the lifts of a given u_S form a torsor under T_0^I.

On the next page this is globalised. For a topological group G acting differentiably on (X,I), one sets G̃ = {(u,ũ)}, with the topology of convergence of u and uniform convergence of ũ. This gives an extension 1 → T_0^I → G̃ → G → 1, which is a covering. A marginal note says that G acts on T_0^I through the orientation character (and, implicitly, by permuting I).

For G = Diff^+(X,I) fixing I pointwise, π_0(G̃) is the mapping class group of the surface obtained by real blow-up at the points of I, i.e. with |I| boundary circles fixed pointwise. The kernel Z^I is generated by the boundary Dehn twists. This is the 'special Teichmüller group': a Teichmüller group with tangential base points at the punctures. It is the topological counterpart of the central extension Γ_{g,[n] with boundary} → Γ_{g,n}, and the discrete analogue of the Ẑ(1)^I extension relevant for tangential base points in the Galois-action story.
errors: No mathematical error on this page itself. A minor slip: the automorphism is said to be of '(X,S)' where '(X,I)' is meant, since S is defined only afterwards from I.

The identification of the deck group of S̃_i with a single T_0 needs the orientation of X, or the twist by the orientation character. The page only says 'module d'orientation'; the next page's NB makes this precise.

The claim (next page) that G̃ → G is a covering implicitly uses local contractibility of Homeo(S^1), or local sections of the universal cover of Homeo^+(S^1) over Homeo^+(S^1). This is true but not stated.

ideas.what: Circles of tangent half-lines at marked points, used as replacement for punctures (real oriented blow-up / tangential base points)
ideas.modern_name: real oriented blow-up; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, tangential base points); real blow-up is classical (A'Campo, Kato–Nakayama in log geometry)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller groups of surfaces with boundary and 'points base' at infinity, but not this exact construction

ideas.what: Extension 1 → T_0^I → G̃ → G → 1 obtained by lifting the derivative action on direction circles to their universal covers; the set of lifts is a T_0^I-torsor
ideas.modern_name: mapping class group of surface with boundary as central Z^n extension of punctured mapping class group (boundary Dehn twists); framed/special Teichmüller groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in mapping class group theory (Birman, Harer, etc.); Milnor/Wood for the universal cover of Homeo^+(S^1)
ideas.where_published: Related remarks on 'groupes de Teichmüller' with boundary appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); exact construction unsure

ideas.what: Orientation module T_0 (π_1 of circle, Z twisted by orientation) as discrete analogue of Ẑ(1)
ideas.modern_name: orientation sheaf / Tate twist analogy Z(1) ↔ Ẑ(1)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4/SGA 5 (Tate twists); La Longue Marche (orientation module)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, careful set-up of mapping class groups with tangential data at the marked points, via real blow-up circles and their universal covers. It gives the standard Z^I extension by boundary twists. These are well-known objects; the page only opens the section, before any proposition is stated.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit ũ un autom. diff. de (X,S)' should most likely read 'Soit u un autom. diff. de (X,I)': the tilde belongs to the lifts, and the pair is (X,I).
The section number at top left ('53') is underlined and has a superscript-like mark; it may be '5 3/4' or a sub-numbering rather than '53' (uncertain).

In the margin addition, 'compacte' is struck out in favour of 'différentiable' above it, with 'orientable' added. The phrase 'compacte dans le cas qui nous intéresse' is inserted in parentheses after 'connexe'. The transcription's bracketing is essentially right.
